A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SurrogateSHAP study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated algorithms and counterfactual results.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffusion-model experiments, synthetic Shapley simulations, counterfactual evaluations, and a dermatology auditing case study in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds independent-training reference results, surrogate-architecture comparisons, and baseline hyperparameter analyses.

M1.justification: The conditional-mixture proxy, Shapley-kernel sampling, XGBoost surrogate objective, and interventional TreeSHAP procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is condensed and moved into the main text. The ArtBench training revision concerns the experimental target model rather than the proposed attribution procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CIFAR-20 subset, ArtBench Post-Impressionism artworks, Fashion-Product brands, ISIC hospital data, and synthetic coalition games. The added analyses use existing datasets and tasks without introducing new populations or test scenarios.

E2.justification: New Appendix E.3 compares the XGBoost surrogate against linear regression, a two-layer MLP, and random forest in Table S.7. The attribution-method comparator roster in Table 2 remains unchanged; Witter et al. is newly discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and the implementation appendix replace ArtBench's rank-256 LoRA training with full fine-tuning, a substantive reported protocol revision that does not establish which experiments were rerun. v2 also introduces independent-training controls, five-fold surrogate-architecture comparisons, and TRAK/D-TRAK regularization sweeps at projection dimensions 4,096 and 32,768.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantive checks of surrogate architecture choice and baseline hyperparameter sensitivity in Appendix E.3–E.4, plus independent-training reference comparisons for proxy fidelity in Section 5.2. These address previously untested design and comparison questions. Existing synthetic, counterfactual, and clinical analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 5.2 newly reports comparisons between independently trained original-game instances using different random seeds, contextualizing training variability in Table 1 without specifying an increased run count. Existing five-seed confidence intervals, counterfactual standard deviations, and 60-trial synthetic evaluations remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises numerous ArtBench LDS means, including SurrogateSHAP from 44.14% to 39.0% and D-TRAK from -20.75% to -8.75%; the reported training change prevents interpreting these as same-setting performance changes. Fashion LPIPS LDS changes from 12.52% to 18.52% for TRAK and from -2.82% to 15.82% for D-TRAK. Table 1 adds training-reference scores, while Table S.7 and Figure S.15 add architecture and sensitivity results. Relocated counterfactual results are retained.

T1.justification: The stability assumption, Proposition 4.2 error bound, Shapley error decomposition, and Appendix B proof remain unchanged in substance. v2 explicitly identifies the coalition-specific prior and mixture already used in v1's proxy definition; the accompanying revisions clarify the existing mathematics rather than introduce a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: training-free coalition evaluation, tree-based Shapley estimation, improved attribution efficiency, and clinical auditing. Replacing 'retraining game' with 'training game' does not broaden the original definition, which already included fine-tuning.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits applicability to settings without overlapping contributor prompt spaces, expands the interpretation of the stability bound, and removes the assertion that the error decomposition itself ensures theoretically controlled errors. It also strengthens the pruning interpretation to preserving downstream utility, although the retained CIFAR-20 results still show FID increases.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link, specifies coalition budgets of 600, 700, and 800 in Table 2, and reports average cross-validation runtimes of 0.86, 1.65, and 26.62 seconds. The ArtBench implementation description is revised from LoRA to full fine-tuning; most other implementation and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4.2 newly positions the method alongside Witter et al.'s direct tree-surrogate Shapley estimation and Monte Carlo residual correction. The dermatology appendix supplies the previously unresolved Combalia et al. citation, and the Hu et al. LoRA reference is removed. The broader related-work framing remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes training terminology, refines the contributor setup and theoretical explanations, moves Algorithm 1 into the main text, and discusses bottom-removal before top-removal counterfactuals. It also adds acknowledgments and makes localized language corrections. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains shaded training-reference rows, Table 2 is enlarged, and a new architecture table and sensitivity figure appear in the appendix. v1's bottom-removal Table S.7 becomes v2's main Table 3, while the former main top-removal table moves to Table S.8. Existing plots and qualitative examples are otherwise preserved.

improvement.justification: The added training controls, architecture comparison, and baseline sensitivity analysis provide useful validation missing from v1, while explicit budgets, runtimes, code-access information, and applicability limits improve transparency. These gains outweigh localized reporting defects, but the improvement is limited: v2's Section 5.4 still quotes ArtBench LDS values of 44.14% and -20.75% despite Table 2 changing them to 39.0% and -8.75%, leaving the revised results inconsistently documented.
